physics-h3-c.material: [Advanced 2D mechanics] For projectile wey dem shoot from ground with initial speed v₀ for angle θ with di horizontal, di maximum horizontal range R na R = (v₀² sin 2θ) / g. If no air resistance dey, wetin be di launch angle θ wey go make di horizontal range maximum, and wetin be di other launch angle wey get di same horizontal distance as launch angle 30°?

physics-killer-12.title: Two parallel conductor rails
physics-killer-12.goal: Apply principles to solve the inquiry problem.
physics-killer-12.material: Two parallel conductor rails wey get spacing $\ell=0.5\,\mathrm{m}$ dey for horizontal surface, and one end connect with resistor. Di total resistance of di closed circuit wey rails, conducting bar and resistor form na $2\,\Omega$. Uniform vertical magnetic field $B=0.5\,\mathrm{T}$ dey cover di whole circuit, and di conducting bar dey move for di rails with constant speed $4\,\mathrm{m/s}$ away from di resistor. While di bar move $0.5\,\mathrm{s}$ during $2\,\mathrm{m}$, di magnetic flux wey dey pass through di circuit change by $\Delta\Phi=B\ell\Delta x$. Which one correctly match, in order, di strength of di induced current for di circuit and di size of di external force wey dem need to keep di bar for constant speed? (No friction dey.)
physics-killer-12.s.s1.prompt: Two parallel conductor rails wey get spacing $\ell=0.5\,\mathrm{m}$ dey for horizontal surface, and one end connect with resistor. Di total resistance of di closed circuit wey rails, conducting bar and resistor form na $2\,\Omega$. Uniform vertical magnetic field $B=0.5\,\mathrm{T}$ dey cover di whole circuit, and di conducting bar dey move for di rails with constant speed $4\,\mathrm{m/s}$ away from di resistor. While di bar move $0.5\,\mathrm{s}$ during $2\,\mathrm{m}$, di magnetic flux wey dey pass through di circuit change by $\Delta\Phi=B\ell\Delta x$. Which one correctly match, in order, di strength of di induced current for di circuit and di size of di external force wey dem need to keep di bar for constant speed? (No friction dey.)
physics-killer-12.s.s1.explain: $\Delta\Phi=B\ell\Delta x=0.5\cdot0.5\cdot2=0.5\,\mathrm{Wb}$, $|\mathcal E|=\dfrac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}=\dfrac{0.5}{0.5}=1.0\,\mathrm{V}$ (e match as $=B\ell v=0.5\cdot0.5\cdot4$). $I=\dfrac{\mathcal E}{R}=\dfrac{1.0}{2}=0.5\,\mathrm{A}$. Di magnetic force wey dey act on di bar na $F=BI\ell=0.5\cdot0.5\cdot0.5=0.125\,\mathrm{N}$ (di direction wey dey oppose di motion according to Lenz's law) and because e constant speed, di external force na $0.125\,\mathrm{N}$ too. Check: power of di external force $Fv=0.125\cdot4=0.5\,\mathrm{W}=I^2R=0.25\cdot2$. If you forget $\ell$ e be $I=1.0\,\mathrm{A}$ (wrong answer ①), if you forget $\ell$ for di force e be $0.25\,\mathrm{N}$ (wrong answer ②), and di mistake of multiplying $\mathcal E$ with $\frac12$ na wrong answer ④.
physics-killer-12.s.s2.prompt: Which scenario demonstrates the correct real-world application of this principle?
physics-killer-12.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.
